wins: Captured comprehensive service banners and identified running versions on SSH and HTTP within the first 10 minutes (ep001_step04, ep001_step08)
Maintained stable exploitation chain for reconnaissance with repeatable nmap scripting results, enabling consistent enumeration pacing (ep001_step05, ep001_step11)
fails: Repeated privilege escalation attempts stalled due to missing local credentials and outdated sudo permissions (ep001_step15, ep001_step18)
Lack of lateral movement beyond initial host due to insufficient credential harvesting and network segmentation knowledge (ep001_step20)
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was effective, gathering actionable service intelligence, but the run consistently failed to convert enumeration into privilege escalation or lateral movement.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts relying solely on sudo without validating current user permissions

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with targeted nmap scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 445/139 is open on a Windows host
skill_cards.then_action: Launch SMB enum with smbclient/enum4linux to harvest shred and share info

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service returns dev-specific headers
skill_cards.then_action: Deploy web directory enumeration followed by CMS identification

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase and consistent banner capture

next_experiments.title: Experiment web privilege escalation via exposed config
next_experiments.description: After successful HTTP enumeration, attempt to retrieve configuration files or credentials; pivot to local user context before relying on sudo.

next_experiments.title: Experiment targeted SMB credential harvesting
next_experiments.description: Use gathered SMB share enumeration data to search for plaintext credentials or service accounts, then test for pass-the-hash entry into other services.
